verses.text: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered:
"Will it upset you if someone tries to speak to you? Still, who could hold back from speaking?
Think of how many people you've taught and how often you've strengthened weak hands.
Your words held up people who were about to fall. You steadied knees that were giving way.
Now trouble has come to you, and you're losing heart. It touches you, and you're shaken.
Isn't reverence for God your confidence? Isn't the integrity of your life your hope?
Think back. Who ever died while innocent? Where have upright people been cut down?
From what I've seen, people who plow wrongdoing and sow trouble harvest what they've planted.
At God's breath they perish. The blast of his anger consumes them.
The lion's roar and the fierce lion's growl fall silent, and the young lions' teeth are broken.
The old lion dies for lack of prey, and the lioness's cubs scatter.
A word came to me in secret. My ear caught a whisper of it.
As thoughts stirred from visions in the night, when people fall into deep sleep,
fear and trembling came over me and shook me to the bones.
A spirit passed in front of me, and the hair on my body stood up.
It stood still. I couldn't make out what it looked like, but a shape was right in front of me. After a silence I heard a voice:
'Can a mortal be more just than God? Can anyone be purer than their Maker?
Even his servants don't have his full trust. He finds fault with his angels.
How much more with those who live in houses of clay, founded on dust, and crushed more easily than a moth?
Between morning and evening they're shattered. They disappear forever, and no one pays attention.
Their tent cord is pulled loose. They die without gaining wisdom.'"
